messages:
Alex: quick flag - noticed a p95 regression on streaming responses after the kernel-selector rollout (canary).
Priya: ack. saw alerts too. is it only streaming or regular batch as well?
Alex: mostly streaming. non-streamed generation p95 stable. profiling shows extra slow path in kernel fallthrough when seq_len <= 64 and token_budget small.
Mateo: can you paste the profiling snippet? curious if it's the kernel shim or the queueing metadata.
Alex: here are the hot spots from perf trace (shortened):
```
0. [13.2%] kernel_selector::choose_fused_attention (fallback path)
1. [11.7%] batch_coalescer::emit_partial_flush
2. [9.4%] kv_cache::warmup_if_needed
3. [7.1%] stream_writer::flush_async
```
Seems like we fall into fallback kernels due to token budget gating, which then triggers more frequent partial flushes.
Priya: sounds like our token_target heuristic (auto=32) is too aggressive for streamed short outputs. We probably want higher token_target for streams or a different eval for expected response length.
Jun: ops note - customers on dedicated infra reported jitter 50-120ms increase p95 last 24h. rollback might be needed if canary spreads.
Alex: proposing an experiment: 1) bump stream token_target to 96, 2) increase coalesce max_delay_ms from 12->20 for streaming route, 3) add a fast-path kernel hint when seq_len<48 and kv_warmup true. small A/B.
Mateo: +1. also try disabling preemptive partial_decode for streams under 20 tokens; that preempt seems to cause extra kernel handoffs.
Priya: agreed. adding metrics to capture kernel_choice label and partial_decode_count per request. we need to correlate kernel_choice with latency and cost.
Alex: config snippet for the experiment: 
```json
{
  "route": "streaming-compact",
  "heuristics": {
    "token_target": 96,
    "max_delay_ms": 20,
    "partial_decode_preempt_ms": 0,
    "prefer_fused_kernel": true
  }
}
```
We can roll to 10% traffic.
infra-bot: deploy started: rollout streaming-heuristic-v2 -> 10% (canary). CI checks passed.
Jun: monitoring dashboards: added kernel_choice heatmap and kv_warmup latency series. will watch p50/p95 and partial_decode_rate.
Priya: also add a tiny microbenchmark: synthetic short-streams (avg tokens=8) vs long-streams (avg tokens=120) to validate heuristics.
Alex: after 20m canary we'll compare: key metrics p95 latency, kernel_fallback_rate, token_cost_per_resp, partial_decode_count.
Mateo: if fallback_rate drops but cost rises, might still be net positive because latency SLO matters for streams. keep cost telemetry though.
Alex: if canary looks good i'll promote and open follow-up to tune dynamic token_target based on recent client history (adaptive per-connection).
Priya: one more thought: KV warmup is audible—maybe we can warm KV asynchronously earlier for streams predicted to need it. add warmup window to admission.
Jun: noted, creating incident watch in case regressions spike. will post alerts to #incidents if p95 > baseline + 30ms.
Alex: thanks all — will post quick results update in 20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
